title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: It's the weekend — U.S. markets are closed with no new escalation confirmed since Friday's close. Fri 10/23: Dow -1.2% (-653 pts), S&P 500 -0.5%, Nasdaq -0.2% as Brent crude hit $116.72/bbl (highest settle since April) and WTI jumped ~4% to $103.48; 10-yr Treasury yield near 5%, gold -1.2%.
Markets: Oil stayed bid into the weekend on Iran's threat to strike U.S. bases, warships and civilian targets in Gulf countries if the U.S. and Israel resume attacks.
Companies: American Express cut 5% of its workforce to speed decision-making while raising its full-year profit outlook; shares still fell 3.7% Friday, the worst performer on the Dow.

Companies: SK Hynix scrapped U.S. IPO plans for flash-memory unit Solidigm citing market conditions, after a South Korean data-center IPO flopped (-30% on debut); Anthropic's IPO is still expected in November.
Macro/Policy: Week ahead — the Fed meets Wednesday for its next rate decision; a heavy earnings slate follows with Alphabet, Microsoft, ExxonMobil, Chevron, Coca-Cola and GE Vernova reporting.

Macro/Policy: Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are reportedly en route to the U.S. under Trump's deal with Moscow; lawmakers from both parties question whether the imports violate a 2022 law barring Russian oil/refined products.

Macro/Policy: Trump signed an executive order citing national-security risk from imported wind-turbine parts but stopped short of new tariffs, opting instead for 180 days of trade talks with partners (Bloomberg).

Macro/Policy: Diesel prices remain near record highs amid Iran-war supply disruptions; Trump unveiled $8B in one-time farmer relief aid, and DOE is freeing up $150M to restart/expand domestic refining capacity.
